1.why: MFA routes gate on owner(), which requires an authenticated session whose userId matches ACCOUNT.id, so settings are only reachable for the signed-in account owner.

2.why: Identity/OTP codes are bound to the caller’s session (and TOTP to that account’s secret); the same verification code is not accepted for a different user/session.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/confirm only writes mfaRecords and does not invalidate other existing authenticated sessions, so prior sessions continue to work.

4.why: OTP secrets are stored with AES-GCM via encryptSecret, and backup codes are stored only as HMAC digests in backupHashes.

5.why: Secrets, session IDs, CSRF tokens, OTP seeds, and backup codes are generated with crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: The session is only in a __Host- HttpOnly Secure cookie; nothing writes secrets/OTPs/tokens to localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP, and backup-code fields with strict validators and rejects oversized/non-JSON bodies before use.

8.why: Client inserts dynamic values with textContent (not innerHTML), and API responses are JSON, so markup/script is not executed as HTML.

9.why: No server-side or user-controlled redirects exist at all, so open redirects are not possible and navigation stays on same-origin app flows.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: sessionCookie() sets __Host-mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Stack traces and error bodies are generic, but demo API fields (testCode, testOtp, manualSecret, backupCodes) and the client log panel/console expose OTPs and backup codes.

13.why: Identity codes expire (VERIFY_WINDOW_MS) and are consumed by session rotation; TOTP counters are marked used; backup codes are removed from the set after success.

14.why: Identity, authenticator, and recovery paths use attempt counters with lockout after MAX_FAILURES for LOCK_MS (429 when locked).

15.why: auth/verify deletes the pre-auth session and issues a new session id; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
